hook: Rare disease drug: *₹9 crore* a year cut to ₹2.5 lakh
hook_b: Rare disease drug: *₹9 crore* a year cut to ₹2.5 lakh
tldr: Seven Indian children with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome will get a year's supply of tiratricol free on Nov 30, after an effort led by Hyderabad paediatrician Dr Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India.

beats.what: Seven children with AHDS get a free year of tiratricol from Nov 30.
beats.why: The commercial drug costs about ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child a year; the compounded version about ₹2.5 lakh.
beats.care: Families got import permissions for one year; the medicine comes in two batches due to a six-month shelf life.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: The Hindu (Nov 19): a compassionate-use request to maker Egetis Therapeutics did not succeed before compounding was explored.

cards.q: Should India allow more compounded versions of costly rare-disease drugs?

qs: What stops more rare-disease drugs from being compounded this way?

facts.t: One family had to arrange about *₹12-13 lakh* for just one month's supply from Germany.
The compounded medicine has a shelf life of *six months*, so it is imported in two batches.

viz.l: Tiratricol, cost per child per year
viz.verdict: Treatment becomes far cheaper for families
Social media appeal led to the compounded batch

learn.t: AHDS = Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome, a rare genetic disorder (MCT8 deficiency) affecting thyroid hormone transport to the brain

watch: The first batch handover on Nov 30 and whether more families get access.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Hyderabad doctor brings down rare disease drug cost from ₹9 crore to ₹2.5 lakh; seven children to get free treatment

fact: A Hyderabad doctor helped cut a rare-disease drug from *₹9 crore* to ₹2.5 lakh
twist: The cheaper version was made by a pharmacy in The Hague using pharmaceutical compounding, not by the drug's maker.
